BrochureContent.Content:
Sion Hill House A Landmark Regency Residence Steeped in Waterford's History

Perched majestically on an elevated 4.7 acre site overlooking Waterford City, Sion Hill House is one of Waterford’s most distinguished period residences. Dating from circa 1820, this elegant Regency style home combines exceptional architectural heritage with breathtaking views, offering a once in a generation opportunity to acquire one of Waterford's finest historic homes.

Sion Hill is steeped in history and was home to the distinguished Pope family during the Cromwellian era and is understood to have remained in their ownership until 1915. The Popes were among Waterford's most respected merchant families, operating trading fleets between Waterford, Europe and America. The property later became a much loved family run guest house and home.

Approached through impressive stone cut entrance gates with a sweeping driveway Sion Hill House is positioned immediate to the Train and Bus stations and is located directly opposite the new pedestrian bridge linking Ferrybank with Waterford City, Sion Hill House occupies an unrivalled position where privacy, history and convenience exist in perfect harmony.

This detached three-bay, two-storey over part-raised basement was built on an L-shaped plan and is rich in character and architectural detail. Two magnificent reception rooms to the front enjoy wonderful views of the River Suir and Waterford City, while a ballroom to the rear provides a spectacular setting for entertaining on a grand scale. The accommodation extends to seven bedrooms and seven bathrooms, offering exceptional flexibility for family living or hospitality.

Outbuildings include charming pavilions, the remains of a former coachman's cottage and coach house.

While the property requires restoration, repair, and ongoing maintenance, it presents a rare opportunity for a discerning purchaser to breathe new life into one of Waterford's most significant historic homes. Rich in character and heritage, Sion Hill is far more than a residence—it is a private and peaceful retreat with remarkable potential. 

In addition, the generous size of the site, combined with its highly desirable city location, offers exciting scope for future development, subject to the necessary planning permissions. Its next custodian has the opportunity to thoughtfully reimagine it as a contemporary family home while also exploring the site's wider potential, carefully balancing modern living with the preservation of its unique character, history, and enduring charm.

Heating is Gas fired, BER exempt.
